raw_response:
I have farmed this land a long time, so I do not start from empty. I start from what worked last year and what I saw around me in Quzhou. Wheat and maize are still my main eating-money crops, and with my well water I will not let them dry if I can help it. On 20 mu, I have to watch cost, but if I cut fertilizer too much and lose yield, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. So I will keep the wheat-maize land steady and put the rest in cotton. For wheat, I will use the stronger base dressing and then topdress once when it turns green, because around here that is the safe way to keep heads full. For maize after wheat, I will not be stingy with nitrogen, because if maize goes pale later it is hard to catch back up. Cotton I will keep on a smaller block, use a bit less nitrogen than maize, more potash than wheat, and spray more times because bugs on cotton can turn bad fast. I do what I have seen hold yield in nearby fields: plough before wheat and cotton, rotary after wheat for maize, water when the crop truly needs it, and keep inputs on the safe side rather than gambling on a thin application.
